decisions.reason: The source message separately reiterates underside serviceability, but that effect is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The mention of splash control at higher RPMs reiterates the candidate's existing high-speed splash constraint without changing its value or scope.
Praise for the integrated form factor and curved tower design does not change the existing enclosure form-factor requirement.
The upper-tower rigidity requirement does not alter the prototype's off-the-shelf electrical-component strategy.
The source discusses visible plumbing integration but does not change any leak-prevention or sealing requirement.
Approval of the curved tower and spout appearance does not necessarily modify the spout's recorded geometry, orientation, material, or pour direction.
The structural-rigidity concern does not change the raised platform's height, footprint, cup support, or clearance purpose.
Mechanical vibration of the upper tower does not change the electrical load, controller, power-supply, or overload-protection requirements.
The source does not request a BOM revision or change any selected component; addressing tower rigidity may require engineering work but no component-list change is entailed.
The source's vibration concern and splash reminder do not change the recorded mixing, frothing, whisk, or high-speed smoothness criteria.
Upper-tower rigidity while running does not alter whisk removability, detachment behavior, or tool-free-removal preference.
The source does not change bowl removal, swapping, or clearance behavior.
